label: State and initialization
definitions: q: generalized positions (hinges in rad, sliders in m); q̇: velocities (rad/s or m/s); a: activation (0–1); l_f: muscle fiber lengths (m); ξ: two-dimensional pad shear displacement (m). The saved initial state x₀ includes posture, velocity, activation, fiber length and shear memory. It is applied once; no resets occur at stride boundaries.

label: Prescribed periodic excitation
definitions: i: muscle channel; uᵢ: applied dimensionless excitation (0–1); Uᵢ: linearly interpolated fixed input table; t: simulation time (s); T: input period, 0.6833333333 s; frac: fractional part of the cycle. The same prescribed excitation cycle repeats throughout the calculation, independently of motion and forces.

label: Activation dynamics
definitions: aᵢ: activation (0–1); uᵢ: excitation (0–1); τ_act and τ_deact: activation and deactivation time constants (s), from activation.py. q and Ground_Reaction_Forces do not enter this input law. Native MuJoCo integrates activation. The equation is the unsmoothed branch; switch_smoothing_width is also exposed in the parameters. The current values are checked in the parameter table.

label: Path length and fiber–tendon partition
definitions: L_MT: whole muscle–tendon length (m), not fiber length; L_path: routed origin/via/wrap/insertion length (m); ΔL: fixed path-length offset (m); l_T: tendon length (m); l_f: fiber length (m); α: constant pennation angle. Editable attachment coordinates are local to their named bones. Source pulley routing and native wrapping are described in the attachment map.
reference: Source geometry: Rahmati et al.; user Model 3 parameters. Elastic extension is a project addition.

label: Normalized fiber variables
definitions: λ: dimensionless normalized fiber length; ν: normalized fiber velocity, positive when lengthening; l_opt: optimal fiber length (m); v_max: positive maximum-shortening-speed magnitude in optimal lengths/s. l_opt v_max is a physical speed in m/s.

label: Active force–length curve
definitions: f_L: dimensionless active force–length multiplier; λ: normalized fiber length; ρᵢ: channel-specific exponent. The constants 1.55 and 0.55 are editable in formulation_constants.py. The applied muscle parameters select the source MATLAB curve rather than the unused generic piecewise fallback.

label: Applied smooth force–velocity curve
definitions: f_V: dimensionless velocity multiplier; ν: normalized fiber velocity; d₁ = −0.3211346128, d₂ = −8.149, d₃ = −0.374, d₄ = 0.8825327733. Current channels enable this curve. Source shortening/lengthening coefficients remain available but inactive when this flag is 1. Excursions outside the stated normalized domain [−1,1] are diagnostics, not validated muscle behavior.
reference: De Groote et al. (2016); corrected coefficients from OpenSim. This is explicitly an adaptation of the original cat muscle law.

label: Optional source velocity curve
definitions: cᵢ and eᵢ: dimensionless source-shortening and source-lengthening curvature values in muscle_tendon.py; ν: normalized fiber velocity. This branch is used only if degroote_force_velocity_enabled is 0. It is retained for transparent inspection; changing that flag creates a different mechanical model requiring a new trial.

label: Passive fiber force
definitions: f_PE: passive tension normalized by maximum isometric muscle force F0; lambda = l_f/l_opt is normalized fiber length, dimensionless. All 104 current channels (28 hindlimb and 76 forelimb) have passive_fiber_enabled = 1. The branch contributes zero when lambda <= 1 and positive tension when lambda > 1. Published coefficients 0.0075 and 11.6 are from Prilutsky et al. (2016), Table 10.3, and Rahmati et al. (2025), Table 3. Rectification to prevent compression and the exponent cap of 50 are implementation adaptations. The same normalized law is extended to added toe/girdle channels; this is not a measurement of each channel's passive force curve. F_PE = F0 f_PE is included inside fiber/tendon equilibrium.

label: Elastic tendon law
definitions: ε: tendon strain; l_T: tendon length (m); l_s: slack tendon length (m); f_T: normalized tension; ε₀: strain at maximum isometric muscle force; ε_toe: toe-region transition strain; k = 3: exponential toe curvature. This custom exponential-to-linear tendon law is an implementation assumption, not an identified tendon law for every cat muscle.

label: Continuous tendon transition
definitions: ε_toe and ε₀: dimensionless strains; k: toe curvature; F_T: tendon tension (N); F₀: maximum isometric muscle force (N). This choice makes force and slope continuous at the transition and gives f_T(ε₀)=1. Do not multiply F₀ by cos α again.

label: Fiber–tendon equilibrium and time discretization
definitions: βᵢ: normalized fiber damping coefficient; n: time-step index; h: integration step (s); all force-balance terms are dimensionless tendon-direction forces. Safeguarded Newton iteration with bisection fallback solves for l_f at each step. Fiber bounds and residuals are reported. Pennation enters length geometry; the force scale is tendon-projected. This is a massless series equilibrium model.

label: Generalized muscle force and moment arms
definitions: j: generalized coordinate; rᵢⱼ: signed moment arm (m for a rotational coordinate, dimensionless for a translational coordinate); Q_m: summed generalized muscle force (N m for a hinge, N for a slider). Individual contributions rᵢⱼF_T are saved separately. They exclude passive joint forces, contact and joint reactions. Source moving-route geometry was checked by a virtual-work audit.

label: Normal contact at each pad
definitions: p: one of 24 pads (six per paw); δ: indentation (m); R: pad radius (m); z: world pad-center height (m) above a ground plane at zero; k_n: normal coefficient (N/m^(3/2)); c_n: dissipation (s/m); v_z: contact-point vertical velocity (m/s), positive upward; F_z: nonnegative vertical force (N). No measured GRF is imposed.
reference: Normal-law concept: Hunt & Crossley (1975). Fitted constants are effective contact parameters, not measured paw tissue properties.

label: Tangential trial force
definitions: ξ: tangential pad displacement (m); v_t: contact-point tangential velocity (m/s); h: timestep (s); b_t: shear damping (N s/m); δ_d = 0.001 m: damping ramp depth; k_t: shear stiffness (N/m); T*: trial tangential force (N). This is a Kelvin–Voigt shear element combined with a friction slider.

label: Friction limit and slip return
latex: \mathbf F_t=-\mathbf T^*\min\!\left(1,\frac{\mu F_z}{\|\mathbf T^*\|}\right),\quad\gamma=\frac{[\|\mathbf T^*\|-\mu F_z]_+}{k_t h+b_{eff}},\quad\boldsymbol\xi^{n+1}=\boldsymbol\xi^*-h\gamma\frac{\mathbf T^*}{\|\mathbf T^*\|}
definitions: F_t: tangential contact force (N); μ: dimensionless friction coefficient; [x]₊ = max(0,x); γ: slip-speed correction (m/s). Zero force is handled separately to avoid division by zero. Shear memory resets when the pad unloads. This project’s discrete return map is not MuJoCo’s native friction solver.

label: Paw resultant and body wrench
latex: \mathbf F_{paw}=\sum_{p\in paw}\mathbf F_p,\qquad\boldsymbol\tau_b=\sum_{p\in b}(\mathbf x_p-\mathbf c_b)\times\mathbf F_p
definitions: F_paw: resultant GRF (N); F_p: individual pad force (N); x_p: world contact point (m); c_b: body center of mass (m); τ_b: contact moment about that center (N m). Six pad forces are applied to each paw through the same multibody system. Native collisions are disabled for the custom pads to avoid double counting; body-ground collisions still identify a fall.

label: Coupled multibody dynamics
latex: \mathbf M(\mathbf q)\ddot{\mathbf q}+\mathbf b(\mathbf q,\dot{\mathbf q})=\mathbf Q_m+\mathbf Q_{passive}+\mathbf J_c^T\mathbf F_c+\mathbf Q_{constraint}
definitions: M: generalized mass matrix; b: gravity, Coriolis and centrifugal terms; q̈: generalized acceleration; Q_m: muscle forces/moments; Q_passive: passive joint spring/damping forces; J_c: contact Jacobian; F_c: contact forces; Q_constraint: native joint-limit/other constraint forces. All four limbs are mechanically coupled through M, the torso and contacts. The planar root translates forward/vertically and pitches; lateral balance is excluded.

label: Passive joint forces
definitions: kⱼ: passive joint stiffness (N m/rad for hinges, N/m for sliders); bⱼ: joint damping (N m s/rad or N s/m); q_ref: resting position (rad or m). This expression describes configured spring/damping terms; native limit/friction constraints remain separate. These are mechanical effects, not excitation corrections.

label: Anatomical angle conventions
definitions: θ_H and θ_F: source sagittal anatomical angle conventions (rad; displayed/exported also in degrees); q: native hinge angles. The same transforms are applied to the predictions and references. The left-hind reference includes the saved assembly correction and is explicitly assumed rather than measured.

label: Fixed reference clocks
definitions: s: limb order LH, RH, LF, RF; φ: reference cycle phase; T: common period (s); Δ: fixed phase offsets. The forelimb original period was 0.6878574832 s. These are comparison conventions, not phase shifts optimized separately to improve a plotted result. No dynamic time warping or filtering is used.

label: Reported errors and display normalization
definitions: y: a particular angle or force channel; y_ref: corresponding fixed-clock reference; N: compared samples; RMSE: root mean squared error in that channel’s units. ũ and ã: optional GUI display values divided by the same fixed intact input peak (with a 0.02 denominator floor). EMG is independently peak-normalized. Raw u and a are saved without this display rescaling.
